clue.text: Brings in reductions — in confusion

indicators.note: letters in confusion are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A manager announces cuts to a baffled, disordered workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brings in reductions' reads as one phrase about cutbacks; the definition stops after 'Brings in', and 'reductions' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce something is to bring it in, as a new rule or a guest.

clue.text: Everyman will start to specify afflictions

parts.note: the setter speaking: I'll, apostrophe dropped. The same letters also run on unbroken across neighbouring clue words, a coincidence of the pieces sitting side by side; the setter gives no hidden-word signal.

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The setter promises to begin listing his complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves by name, so 'Everyman will' is 'I will', shortened to I'LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ills are troubles or ailments, the things that afflict you.

clue.text: Skipping intro, make-up of rock music's smallest section?

indicators.note: skipping the intro drops the word's opening letter

parts.note: stone is what rock is made of; minus its first letter S

explanation.surface: A listener skips a rock track's intro to find its tiniest musical fragment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock music' looks like a genre, but 'rock' belongs to the wordplay and 'music's smallest section' is the definition. The question mark flags that a tone is only loosely the smallest step.
explanation.definitionFit: A tone is a basic interval between notes, one of the small units a scale is built from.

clue.text: A joke that's been told often? Told ten such, sadly

definitions.text: A joke that's been told often?

indicators.note: things gone sadly wrong are out of order

explanation.surface: Someone groans at a stale gag, having heard ten of them already.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter reuses 'told' on purpose: the first one sits in the definition, the second starts the fodder, so the two sentences read as one weary comment.
explanation.definitionFit: An old chestnut is a joke or story repeated so often it has grown stale.

clue.text: Not identified, curiously mundane …

indicators.note: letters arranged curiously are in an odd order

explanation.surface: Something anonymous is, oddly, also rather dull, and the thought trails into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue's surface to 5 down; they carry no wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnamed has not been given a name, so it is not identified.

clue.text: … getting flat later in the day

definitions.note: 'later in the day' is a phrase for the time, answered by the noun
definitions.meaning: the verb 'even' (make level) with -ing, as in levelling out a lawn
the time of day between afternoon and night

explanation.surface: Carrying on from 4 down: something dull that goes flat as the day wears on, like a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first sense as the verb 'even' plus -ing, as in evening out a lawn; the time of day hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening is both making something level and the part of the day after afternoon.

clue.text: Characters in the picture Gladiator, for example

indicators.note: the answer's characters, its letters, sit in the words that follow

explanation.surface: A film buff lists the characters in the film Gladiator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like the cast list of the film, but here it means letters. Gladiator is the 2000 Russell Crowe film.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiator is a sweeping historical film, the kind called an epic.

clue.text: Comedian's necessity: drink on the job, son

parts.note: your line is your line of work, your job
s = son, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A comic needs a drink while working, and brings his son along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue means placed above, so the drink sits over the job; 'the job' for a line of work is the step most solvers miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian cannot do without punchlines, the lines that deliver each joke.

clue.text: Reportedly fake aches? Here's some drinks!

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so go by sound

explanation.surface: Someone pretending to be ill is handed a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'sham pains' out loud and it is 'champagnes'; the exclamation mark on 'some drinks' hints at a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagnes are sparkling wines, some drinks in the plural.

clue.text: They're accompanied by country music and silence, bizarrely

indicators.note: letters arranged bizarrely are in a strange order

explanation.surface: Something comes with both country music and silence, which is a strange pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a joining word between two things, but it is part of the fodder; the definition ends at 'music'.
explanation.definitionFit: Line dances are rows of dancers stepping in unison, usually to country music.

clue.text: Woman, one looking unchanged in the mirror

indicators.note: a word that looks the same mirrored reads the same both ways

parts.words: one looking unchanged in the mirror
parts.note: a name that reads the same forwards as backwards, like a reflection

explanation.surface: A woman who never seems to age when she checks her reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks for a woman's name that reads the same forwards and backwards; the surface pretends it is about vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Anna is one of the few common women's names that is a palindrome.

clue.text: Defend vessel in contest

parts.note: to champion a cause is to defend it

explanation.surface: A navy orders its ship defended during a battle at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts the vessel inside the contest, but it only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a championship is a competition, typically a series of rounds, whose winner takes a title.

clue.text: Six men we can corrupt; they're Americans

indicators.note: corrupted letters are spoilt out of their order

explanation.surface: A plotter boasts of six officials they can bribe, all of them American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' reads as a verb about bribery; it only tells you to rearrange the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: New Mexicans live in the US state of New Mexico, so they are Americans.

clue.text: Fats Waller altered natural features

indicators.note: altered letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: The jazz pianist Fats Waller is said to have changed his natural looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Fats Waller was an American jazz pianist; his name is simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: waterfalls are one kind of landscape feature, alongside cliffs and gorges, that nature made.

clue.text: Choosy, wanting item

definitions.meaning: fussy, hard to please about details
a single point or detail, as in 'correct in every detail'

explanation.surface: A fussy shopper hunting for one specific thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The noun sense is the hard one: a particular is an individual point or detail.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular means both fussy about details and, as a noun, one detail or item.

clue.text: Brought together, in a church service, English and Dutch

parts.note: a Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A congregation of English and Dutch worshippers gathered for a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction, but everything simply runs in order after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or bring together in quantity.

clue.text: Looking vacant, initially giving affected wave, His Majesty

indicators.note: initially points to the first letters of the words that follow

parts.note: first letters of Giving Affected Wave

explanation.surface: A monarch gives a bored, mannered royal wave to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected wave' looks like the royal gesture itself; all three words just supply their initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To gawk is to stare stupidly, so gawking is looking vacant.

clue.text: Flies to Niagara, taking in country

indicators.note: the phrase takes the answer in, holding it within its letters

explanation.surface: A traveller flies to Niagara Falls, stopping in another country on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking in' sounds like a sightseeing stop-off; it is the sign that the answer lies inside the phrase before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Estonia is one Baltic state among the world's nations.

clue.text: Not especially impressive batting statistic

definitions.meaning: middling, ordinary, no better than usual
runs scored per dismissal, the standard cricket measure of a batter

explanation.surface: A cricketer's numbers are nothing to write home about.
explanation.walkthrough: A batting average is a batter's runs per dismissal in cricket (in baseball, hits per at-bat).
explanation.definitionFit: Average means ordinary, and it is also the standard measure of a batter's performance.

clue.text: Lead putting energy into public relations? Give up!

parts.note: to cede is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: A PR team is urged to put more energy in, then told to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting energy into public relations' just adds the E on to the end, not inside; the question mark and 'Give up!' make the surface read as a PR pitch dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to go before someone in order or time is to lead them.

clue.text: One choosing to be more generously proportioned?

definitions.meaning: one who plumps for, that is picks, something

explanation.surface: Someone deciding to put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the rare noun: a plumper is one who plumps for, that is picks, something.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumper is both the comparative of plump and a word for someone who plumps for a choice.

clue.text: Side on border; America in charge; take the consequences

parts.note: a facet is one side of a cut gem
a hem is a border on cloth
IC = in charge, as in 2 i/c

explanation.surface: A news report: troops on the border, America in command, and a price to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces cut across the word breaks, so 'Side' is not FACE; the semicolons make it read like a list of headlines.
explanation.definitionFit: To face the music is to accept the unpleasant results of what you did.

clue.text: Ace! It's flipping fizzy wine!

indicators.note: a flipped word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: An excited cry about a bottle of fizz; 'flipping' is the mild British oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' sounds like an exclamation, as in 'flipping brilliant', but it reverses ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Primarily, ferocious animal's nasty gnasher?

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letters of the words that follow

parts.note: first letters of Ferocious Animal's Nasty Gnasher

explanation.surface: A description of a wild beast's vicious tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the four initials spell the very tooth it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A fang is a long sharp tooth of a fierce animal, a nasty gnasher.

clue.text: Three learners maintaining university is quiet

definitions.note: 'quiet' as a noun, a period of calm

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the letters hold the next piece inside

parts.note: L = learner, as on a learner driver's plate; three of them
U = university; held after the first L

explanation.surface: Three students living at a university keep things quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The U goes in after the first L: L(U)LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with 'quiet' as a noun: a lull is a temporary calm, as in a lull in the fighting.

clue.text: Sloshing space, Asian?

indicators.note: sloshing letters slop about into a new order

explanation.surface: A body of water sloshing about in a great Asian expanse.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the Caspian is a vast Asian expanse of sloshing water, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caspian Sea is the huge inland sea between Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Give life to Lord

definitions.meaning: to father offspring, used especially of horses
the old form of address to a king or lord

explanation.surface: A prayer asking the Lord to bring something to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord' looks like God, but it is the title a subject uses to a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sire means both to father offspring and, as a title, my lord.

clue.text: This makes a button do its work? That's sad

definitions.text: This makes a button do its work?

parts.words: This makes a button do its work?
parts.note: pressing a button down is what makes it operate

explanation.surface: A gadget that only works if you push its button, which is a gloomy thought.
explanation.walkthrough: To depress a button is to press it down; the question mark flags this punning sense beside the usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: Depressing is both pushing a button down and causing sadness.
